newsitem.title: USA: Nationsbank buying Montgomery Securities for $1.2 bln.
newsitem.headline: Nationsbank buying Montgomery Securities for $1.2 bln.

text.p: NationsBank Corp. agreed Monday to acquire closely held investment bank Montgomery Securities for $1.2 billion in yet another combination of a commercial bank and a brokerage house.
The acquisition is the latest in a series of moves by financial institutions to snatch up brokerage firms as federal rules prohibiting such deals have been relaxed.
San Francisco-based Montgomery, which specializes in high-technology firms, had made no secret over the past two months of its desire to sell a stake in order to grow the business.
"The combination of our two companies is a great fit and will allow us to reach our goal of providing one-stop shopping to our clients," Montgomery Chief Executive Thomas Weisel said in a statement.

Under terms of the deal, Montgomery will retain substantial autonomy and will become part of NationsBanc Capital Markets Inc., a subsidiary that will be renamed NationsBanc Montgomery Securities Inc. Weisel will become chairman of the unit.

The companies said the purchase will be paid for with a combination of 70 percent cash and 30 percent stock. Montgomery's 68 partners will be paid the cash immediately, with the 30 percent in stock paid over three years.
NationsBank, based in Charlotte, N.C., is the nation's fourth-largest bank, with $239 billion in assets.
"The addition of Montgomery to our organization will create enormous value for our clients," said Ed Brown, president of NationsBank Global Finance.
Brown said the most attractive feature of Montgomery was its equity capabilities, particularly research, something NationsBank has lacked.

"This is the critical missing link for NationsBank, and it is our belief that trying to build this would have been much too time-consuming," Brown said. "This is the last arrow in the quiver that we need to have one-stop financing."

He said that Montgomery's strength in equity and in mergers and aquisitions would complement NationsBank's senior debt and bridge finacing capabilites and help the bank build its middle-market business.
"To be sucessful, you need it all. Now, finally we are in a position where we will be able to offer the total package," Brown said.

Under the pact, NationsBank said it will create a $100 million pool for the long-term retention of key Montgomery non-partner personnel. Half of the funding for the pool will be in stock options and the rest cash. The $100 million pool is in addition to the $1.2 billion payment price.

NationsBank Vice Chairman James Hance said Montgomery's revenues are expected to grow from an estimated $700 million in fiscal 1997 to between $875 million and $900 million in fiscal 1998, adding that those revenues would boost NationsBank's fiscal 1998 earnings by about one cent a share.
"This acquisition will be accretive to earnings immediately beginning day one," he said.
Hance said discussions between the two firms began in early May, with serious negotiations under way by June 10.
Earlier this month, BankAmerica Corp. said it would buy investment bank Robertson Stephens & Co., another San Francisco investment bank, for about $540 million.
In April, Bankers Trust New York Corp. agreed to buy Alex Brown & Sons Inc. for $1.7 billion, and a month later Swiss Bank Corp. agreed to buy Dillon Read & Co. for $600 million.
NationsBank stock rose $1 to $66.25 in consolidated afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
